title: Most conscious thought is a subpersonal process

statements.text: Most of what is called conscious thought is better analyzed as a subpersonal process lacking mental agency, consciously experienced goal-directedness and veto control. Personal-level cognition is the exception, enabled by a model of the system as an epistemic agent. This raises a new version of the mind-body problem: how subpersonal cognition relates causally to personal-level thought.
